WHO WE ARE

Students building the robot,
not just riding along

The Mechatigers are TMSA's FIRST Robotics Competition team, drawing students out of the school's Project Lead the Way engineering program — Engineering Essentials, Introduction to Engineering Design, Principles of Engineering, and Aerospace Engineering. Every year the team takes a new game manual, eight weeks, and a pile of raw stock, and turns it into a robot that has to actually work under pressure, in front of a crowd, on the first try.

Sub-teams cover mechanical design and fabrication, programming in Java, electrical and wiring, strategy and scouting, and business & outreach — so there's a seat for students who want to weld as much as for students who'd rather write code or run the pit.

COMMUNITY & OUTREACH

Passing it down to
the middle schoolers

Mechatigers members also mentor the middle school students on TMSA's campus — running demos, walking them through the robot, and getting them hands-on with the build. The team also shows up for TMSA's community events, running robot exhibitions at the school's fall and spring festivals — teaching community members about robotics through fun, interactive activities.

TMSA fall & spring festivals — Robot Exhibition

HOW A SEASON RUNS

Eight weeks to build,
a season to compete

Every FRC season follows the same arc, from a January reveal to district and regional competition.

Kickoff

FIRST releases the new game. The team spends the first days strategizing, prototyping mechanisms, and picking a robot concept.

Build season

Roughly eight weeks to design, machine, wire, and program the robot — CAD in the evenings, fabrication on weekends.

Competition

The robot ships and the team travels to district and regional events to compete, scout opponents, and iterate between matches.

Off-season

Recruiting, workshops, community demos, and off-season events keep skills sharp before the next kickoff — and after two seasons on the field, a growing list of district results to build on.

WHAT STUDENTS GET OUT OF IT

Real tools, real deadlines

FRC runs on the same disciplines as TMSA's PLTW engineering courses, applied under a real competition clock.

01

Design & fabrication

CAD, sheet metal, machining, and 3D printing turn a strategy sketch into parts that bolt onto the robot.

02

Programming

Students write and test the robot's control code in Java, including autonomous routines and driver-assist features.

03

Strategy & scouting

Reading the game manual for scoring edges, then scouting alliances and calling matches from the pit.
